EnableSdkPluginConfig.description: Controls applying the specified SdkPluginConfigs to generated skill packs. Default: false

SdkPluginConfigs.description: Published SDK package coordinates for each LanguageTemplate. Any field left out falls back to a value derived from the generated SDK. Default: null

PHP_GENERIC_LIB_V2.description: Published package coordinates of the PHP SDK

CS_NET_STANDARD_LIB.description: Published package coordinates of the C# SDK

JAVA_ECLIPSE_JRE_LIB.description: Published package coordinates of the Java SDK

PYTHON_GENERIC_LIB.description: Published package coordinates of the Python SDK

RUBY_GENERIC_LIB.description: Published package coordinates of the Ruby SDK

GO_GENERIC_LIB.description: Published package coordinates of the Go SDK

TS_GENERIC_LIB.description: Published package coordinates of the TypeScript SDK

Repository.description: Source repository of the generated SDK, when it is published to one

Name.description: Published package id — the whole id in TypeScript, Python, Ruby and C#; the artifact or project half in Java and PHP, where Group carries the rest. Overrides the package name the generator derives, since this is what a consumer actually installs. Not parsed: a value like "io.acme:sdk" is taken verbatim as the artifact id. Default: the generated package name

Group.description: Publisher scope of the package id, for the languages whose id is a pair: Maven's groupId in Java, Composer's vendor in PHP. Ignored by TypeScript, Python, Ruby and C#, whose package id is a single name. Default: the group the generator derives from the build

Version.description: Published version of the package. Overrides the version derived from the build, for the same reason Name does: the derived value is whatever the build produced, not necessarily what was released. Load-bearing in Java, where a dependency is the groupId:artifactId:version triple, so a wrong version there is a dependency that fails to resolve rather than a cosmetic error. Taken verbatim, like Name: a configured value is not reshaped, including in C#, where the generated project itself uses a four-part Major.Minor.Patch.0 version. Default: the version derived from the build
